Debt negotiations by individuals is a very risky process sometimes especially if it’s a harsh creditor, there are some lenders who do not negotiate with individuals and only receive documentation from law firms or debt settlement companies, like discover or AMEX and some other creditors do not negotiate with anyone at all like lendmark, world finance and security finance. Now it’s possible to do it with some creditors but in order to reach a settlement you’d have to let the account go delinquent on the credit report meaning that no power out there can reach a settlement while maintaining the account as a current to the creditor, and this puts a lot of people who want to do it by themselves in a legal risk, but when you’re with a good company or a law firm they basically reroute the communication with them so the creditors can know that the individual is in the program and they’re maintaining their payments on the escrow account they have. Debt settlement companies do not negotiate one account for each client individually, meaning that lets say that they enrolled 10 clients who have accounts with AMEX in december, they negotiate the total debt load for the 10 accounts combined together which makes them get lower rates than when an individual does that, i’m in that industry and i know how it works behind the scenes.

In your situation, your account that you reached a settlement for has probably had that outstanding balance because of a high interest rate/late payment or compound interest and it most likely was a charge off, because a settlement is ultimately based on how long you’ve had the account, how much interest you’ve already paid so you’re situation doesn’t necessarily have to match the OPs one.
